therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: HDL-raising via niacin receptor agonism with prostaglandin-mediated flushing suppression by laropiprant
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: HDL cholesterol elevation and cardiovascular risk reduction
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Adults with established cardiovascular disease, peripheral arterial disease, diabetes mellitus, or coronary heart disease on background statin therapy
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Major Vascular Event (non-fatal MI or coronary death, non-fatal or fatal stroke, or revascularisation) over median 3.9 years

results.effect_size: 1696 vs 1758 major vascular events (ER niacin/laropiprant vs placebo); no significant reduction
safety_signals: Increased gastrointestinal serious adverse events in ER niacin/laropiprant arm (620 vs 491)
Increased infections and infestations in ER niacin/laropiprant arm (1031 vs 853)
Increased all-cause mortality in ER niacin/laropiprant arm (798 vs 732)
Increased blood and lymphatic system disorders in ER niacin/laropiprant arm (84 vs 56)

dose_info.dose: ER niacin/laropiprant (dose not individually specified in record); simvastatin 40 mg; ezetimibe 10 mg + simvastatin 40 mg

context.indication: Cardiovascular disease, peripheral arterial disease, diabetes mellitus, coronary heart disease

modulation_entries.hypothesis: ER niacin/laropiprant was hypothesized to amplify cardiovascular risk reduction by raising HDL cholesterol on top of LDL lowering by simvastatin, but the trial showed no additional benefit and possible harm
modulation_entries.citation: ER Niacin/Laropiprant: 1696 major vascular events vs Placebo: 1758 — no significant reduction in major vascular events with addition of ER niacin/laropiprant to statin background therapy
